question: Should OpenClaw add a plugin-visible skill install/update completion observer now, and what redacted payload plus fail-open/fail-closed semantics should it expose after files or metadata are written?
rationale: Automation can prove the missing lifecycle surface and the CLI config propagation gap, but choosing which install metadata plugins may see and whether observer failures can affect an already-written install is a security and product boundary decision.

options.title: Add minimal observer and close coverage gaps
options.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source, target, provenance, outcome, and timestamp metadata, and make sure every OpenClaw-managed install path passes config into the existing blocking policy evaluator.

options.title: Keep blocking policy only
options.body: Declare security.installPolicy and before_install sufficient for install security, fix the CLI config propagation gap if confirmed, and close or narrow the audit-observer request separately.

options.title: Defer to broader ClawHub trust design
options.body: Hold the observer until maintainers define a larger ClawHub trust/provenance API that can supply the same audit events without exposing unsafe local metadata.

recommendation.title: Add minimal observer and close coverage gaps
recommendation.body: Add a non-blocking completion hook with redacted source, target, provenance, outcome, and timestamp metadata, and make sure every OpenClaw-managed install path passes config into the existing blocking policy evaluator.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses native ClawHub install behavior and public plugin lifecycle API shape, where steipete is the strongest history and product-routing signal.
